verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on duties by nature and finding fulfilment in your own work.
verse.sanskrit: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् । स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥
verse.line: Better your own path, imperfectly walked, than someone else's done perfectly.
verse.translation: Better is one's own duty, though imperfect, than the duty of another well performed. Doing the work born of one's own nature, one incurs no wrong.
verse.why: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.
verse.misuse: Not 'stick to the role you were born into'. It's about honest fit with your own nature, not caste or family script.

prasang.title: Duties by nature, and their fruit
prasang.summary: After listing duties by varna, Krishna says one reaches perfection through one's own work done as worship, and that one's own path, though imperfect, beats another's, since every undertaking has flaws.
prasang.lesson: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.

verse.meaning: Krishna is telling Arjuna that the work which fits your own nature is the right work. He says that doing your own duty, even if it is flawed and you stumble along the way, is better than taking on someone else's path and doing it perfectly. The point is that your own work, with all its natural imperfections, is a kind of worship in itself. You do not need to be flawless to be on the right track.
verse.for_you: You have been building apps for years. The doubt you feel is not about the code, but about the question you are asking. Let the work you are doing now be the path, even if it feels imperfect.

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son Sanjaya, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: सर्वेषां कर्मणां तात फले नित्यमनित्यता / अनित्यमिति जानन्तो न भवन्ति भवन्ति च अथ ये नैव कुर्वन्ति नैव जातु भवन्ति ते / ऐकगुण्यमनीहायामभावः कर्मणां फलम्
verse.line: Every result is uncertain. Some who try succeed and some don't. Those who never try never do.
verse.translation: The result of every action is uncertain. Knowing this, some people act and succeed, some do not. But those who never act never succeed at all.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

verse.meaning: Queen Vidula finds her son Sanjaya lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She tells him that the result of every action is uncertain, and some who try succeed while others do not. But those who never try never succeed at all. She is waking him from despair, showing him that the outcome is never guaranteed, yet standing still guarantees nothing.
verse.for_you: The years of side projects are not the failure. The failure is the quiet belief that you could know the exact outcome before you move. You are waiting for certainty in a place where it does not exist. The doubt is not about your skill.

verse.speaker: Ribhu
verse.setting: Ribhu on people of steady goodness.
verse.sanskrit: नापदि ग्लानिमायान्ति निशि हेमाम्बुजं यथा । नेहन्ते प्रकृतादन्यद्रमन्ते शिष्टवर्त्मनि ॥
verse.line: Good people do not wilt in hard times, like a golden lotus that stays open at night.
verse.translation: In adversity they do not wilt, as the golden lotus does not close at night. They want nothing beyond what is at hand and delight in the path of the good.
verse.why: Start with calm or contentment, and the rest follows.

prasang.title: Ribhu on calm and contentment
prasang.summary: Ribhu answers Nidagha: freedom has four gatekeepers (calm, inquiry, contentment and good company), and winning one brings the rest. In a calm mind sorrow and anxiety vanish; restlessness is simply the mind's nature, and only your own mind can lift you out.
prasang.lesson: Start with calm or contentment, and the rest follows.

verse.meaning: Ribhu speaks to Nidagha about people who hold steady. He says that in hard times, a good person does not wilt. They are like a golden lotus that stays open at night, not closing its petals. They want nothing more than what is right in front of them and they find joy in doing what is good. This means you do not need to force yourself to be happy. You only need to start with a calm mind, and the rest of the path will follow naturally.
verse.for_you: You have been running on empty for a long time now. You do not need to force a big breakthrough today. You only need to let the work you have already done stand. The small steps you have taken are enough to keep you from wilting.

verse.speaker: Parvati
verse.setting: Parvati answers the sages who mock her resolve to win Shiva through years of austerity.
verse.sanskrit: सत्य कहेहु गिरिभव तनु एहा। हठ न छूट छूटै बरु देहा॥ कनकउ पुनि पषान तें होई। जारेहुँ सहजु न परिहर सोई ॥
verse.line: Gold comes from stone, and even in fire it stays gold. Hold to what you are.
verse.translation: You speak truly: this body was born of a mountain, so its resolve will not break, even if the body does. Gold too is born of stone, and even in fire it does not give up its nature.
verse.why: Persistence is choosing the same thing again each day, even when others call it foolish.
verse.misuse: Steadiness is not stubbornness; keep checking that the goal is still worth it.

prasang.title: Parvati holds to her choice
prasang.summary: Reborn as Parvati, Sati resolves to marry Shiva and spends years in austerity. The seven sages come to test her, mocking Shiva as a homeless ascetic and offering her a better match. She answers that gold keeps its nature even in fire, and that the heart wants the one it has chosen.
prasang.story_hook: The sages came to talk Parvati out of it, and they listed every flaw in the man she had chosen.
prasang.lesson: Persistence is choosing the same thing again each day, even when others call it foolish.

verse.meaning: Parvati is speaking to the seven sages who have come to mock her choice. She tells them that just as gold is born from stone and does not lose its nature even when it burns in fire, her resolve will not break. The verse asks you to hold to what you are, to let your own nature, your own effort, remain steady even when the heat of doubt is around you.
verse.for_you: You keep going with your apps even when nothing works. That is your nature now. Let it be enough that you are the one who holds to this, even if the result is still hidden.

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: The sage Vasishtha to Bharat, shattered by his father's death and Ram's exile.
verse.sanskrit: तात हृदयँ धीरजु धरहु करहु जो अवसर आजु। उठे भरत गुर बचन सुनि करन कहेउ सबु साजु ॥
verse.line: Keep courage in your heart, and do what today asks of you.
verse.translation: "Child, keep courage in your heart, and do what this moment asks of you today." Hearing his teacher, Bharat rose and had everything made ready.
verse.why: When head and heart disagree, go and face the person you think you wronged.

prasang.title: Bharat refuses the throne
prasang.summary: After the funeral, Vasishtha, the ministers and Kausalya all urge Bharat to rule, as his father wished. Bharat says the advice is right and his heart still isn't at peace; the crown means nothing without Ram. He decides to go to the forest, admit his fault, and trust his brother to forgive.
prasang.story_hook: Everyone agreed the throne was his, and Bharat could not bring himself to sit on it.
prasang.lesson: When head and heart disagree, go and face the person you think you wronged.

verse.meaning: Vasishtha speaks to Bharat after his father's death and Ram's exile. Bharat is shattered, and the court urges him to take the throne. Vasishtha tells him to keep courage in his heart and do what this moment asks of him today. The verse proposes that when your head and heart are in conflict, you could go and face the person you believe you have wronged.
verse.for_you: You have been carrying the weight of what is wrong with your own path. Today, try one small thing that is only for you, and let it be enough.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.setting: Opening verse of 'Advice to the Mind'.
verse.sanskrit: परेषां चेतांसि प्रतिदिवसमाराध्य बहुधा प्रसादं किं नेतुं विशसि हृदय क्लेशकलितम् । प्रसन्ने त्वय्यन्तः स्वयमुदितचिन्तामणिगणो विविक्तः संकल्पः किमभिलषितं पुष्यति न ते ॥
verse.line: Why exhaust yourself daily winning others' approval? Settle inside, and your own clarity grants every wish.
verse.translation: O heart, why do you enter into weariness, day after day trying to please the minds of others in so many ways, to win their favour? When you are at peace within, your own clear resolve rises by itself like a cluster of wish-granting gems: what wish of yours would it not fulfil?
verse.why: Stop seeking approval and rehearsing outcomes; the calm you want is already inside.

prasang.title: Vairagyashatakam: Advice to the mind
prasang.summary: The poet talks to his own mind: why exhaust yourself pleasing others, why replay the past and script the future, why roam everywhere but within. 'So what?' asks what all our gains amount to.
prasang.lesson: Stop seeking approval and rehearsing outcomes; the calm you want is already inside.

verse.meaning: Bhartrihari speaks to his own mind at the opening of his Advice to the Mind. He asks why the mind wears itself out, day after day, trying to please others and win their favour. He says that when you settle inside and find your own peace, your clear resolve rises naturally, like a cluster of wish-granting gems. Then he asks what wish of yours that clarity could not fulfil.
verse.for_you: Your phone holds the noise of everyone else's expectations. Set it down for one hour. Let your own clear resolve rise, and see what it offers you without asking for approval.

story.title: Two old friends meet again and admit they never found peace
story.story_hook: They had been inseparable as boys, and when they met again they were old men with nothing to show.
story.summary: Bhasa and Vilasa grow up inseparable in a forest hermitage. After their fathers die they drift apart and spend long lonely years in hard austerities. When they meet again as old men, one asks if the other is well; he answers honestly that there is no wellness while the mind keeps spinning through endless tasks and worries.
story.lesson: Years of hard effort without inner understanding can leave you exactly where you started.

script: You are carrying a question that has grown as heavy as the duties you already carry. You built apps on the side for years and none of them worked. You keep going, but you do not know what is wrong.
Arjuna is standing on the battlefield. He is paralyzed by grief and doubt. Krishna is beside him, and he is explaining the nature of duty and action. And Krishna replied:
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात्, स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम्.
In plain words: Better your own path, imperfectly walked, than someone else's done perfectly.

Krishna is saying that your own path, even if you stumble and it is imperfect, is better than someone else's path done perfectly. He is not talking about a perfect outcome. He is talking about the work that fits your own nature. Doing it, flaws and all, is the right thing to do. It is a kind of worship. This is easier said than done, because your mind is telling you that you are not good enough. But the act of doing your own work, without comparing it to a perfect standard, is what matters.
Let the work you are doing now be the path, even if it feels imperfect. You do not need to know the whole plan. You only need to take the next small step that is yours.
What if the next step is only to ask one new question?

depth.life: You are carrying work, children, and aging parents, and the years of side projects that have not worked are sitting on top of it. You keep going, but you do not know what is wrong.
depth.points: You are not failing at building. You are failing to find the one question that would make the next step clear, and that question is being asked in the noise of everything else.
depth.practice: Set a timer for ten minutes. Open your work and write down one small question about what you are building right now.
depth.question: What is the one question you have been too tired to ask?
